chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Burayd ibn Mu'awiya al-Ijli who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who set out as a pilgrim, and with him was a camel, expenses, and provisions. If he died in the Haram (sanctuary), his Hajj al-Islam (the obligatory Hajj) sufficed for him. And if he died before entering the state of Ihram, while he was still a 'Sarurah' (one who has not yet performed the obligatory Hajj), his camel, provisions, and expenses are considered part of his obligatory Hajj. If anything remains from that, it belongs to his heirs.

I said: What do you think if the Hajj was voluntary (Nafl), and he died in the way before entering Ihram? Whose would be his camel, expenses, and what he left? He said: It belongs to his heirs, unless he has a debt which is paid off for him, or he made a bequest, in which case that is executed for whom he bequeathed to, and it is taken from the one-third.
And whoever bequeaths a Hajj, and manumission, and other than that, the Hajj should be given priority, then that which follows it among the voluntary acts.

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.حَجَّةُ الْإِسْلاَمِ: The obligatory Hajj, performed once in a lifetime
key_terms.صَرُورَةٌ: One who has not yet performed the obligatory Hajj

ai.seo_question: What happens to a pilgrim's wealth if they die during Hajj before or after entering Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudence of a pilgrim's death en route, establishing that for the obligatory Hajj, the deceased's assets are dedicated to fulfilling the duty, whereas voluntary Hajj assets revert to heirs after settling debts and bequests. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on prioritizing the fulfillment of religious obligations (Hajj) over other bequests, ensuring the spiritual debt is cleared before worldly distribution.
